description:
Add a section to examples/README.md ("Where a wrapper is the right choice") and a paragraph to the verdict's Limitations (defk-sgw.5) with this table, kept short and factual. Each row: the job, the libraries people wrap, why a from-scratch kernel is the wrong tool, and the concrete change that would reopen it. Nothing is excluded on principle; each has a stated condition.

| Job | Wrapped today | Why not from scratch | What would change it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signing, key exchange, secret-dependent crypto (secp256k1, ed25519, X25519, AEAD) | libsodium, secp256k1, ring via Rustler; :crypto | The one rule says nothing about timing. A kernel compiles through clang -O3, which may turn a select into a branch or a table lookup into a secret-dependent access; the runtime cannot promise constant time, and a process dump or a yielded frame holds key material in a resource. Verification with public inputs is allowed but gains little over libsodium. | A constant-time mode: a restricted subset (no secret-dependent branches or indices, checked at compile time), codegen verified with a tool like dudect or ctgrind in CI, frame zeroisation on finish and on process death, and an external audit. Until then: :crypto and the wrappers. |
| Parsers that produce trees or term streams (HTML, Markdown, tree-sitter, general JSON/CSV to terms, protobuf, msgpack) | html5ever, comrak, tree-sitter, jsont, rusty_csv, protox | The product is BEAM terms and building them is the cost: docs/research/string-workloads.md measured a 13x gap between scanning and term creation in Elixir, and a NIF builds terms serially at the same price ("Env is not thread-safe, so term construction is serial", rusty_csv). The kernel cannot build terms, and if it could it would be no faster. | Two things, both measurable: (1) a "tape" output, a flat [i64] of (kind, start, len) events that Elixir turns into terms lazily or into packed columns (the CSV loader ticket defk-9p6.21 is the fused form); worth it only if a real consumer stays packed. (2) Evidence from a benchmark that tape plus Elixir tree building beats Jason or NimbleCSV end to end on a named workload. BPE tokenisation to [i64] ids is the exception: its product is packed; it becomes a Tier 2 candidate after the hash-table work, with the regex pre-tokeniser left in Elixir. |
| Regular expressions | :re (PCRE in C), Rust regex via Rustler | :re is already native and compiled once per pattern; a kernel cannot take a pattern as data without becoming an interpreter, and a fixed-string search is :binary.match (Boyer-Moore in C). | A specific pattern class with a known kernel form (fixed set of literals: :binary.matches already; glob or simple DFA over bytes compiled at Elixir compile time into a kernel table) and a benchmark showing :re loses on it. |
| Large codecs and encoders (brotli, zstd encode, audio and video codecs, PDF/typst rendering) | brotli, zstd, membrane_* FFmpeg/opus bindings, typst | The cost is the spec surface and tuning, not the loop: brotli's static dictionary and context modelling, zstd's multi-level match finders, codecs of 10^4-10^5 lines with SIMD everywhere and patent history. A kernel would be a worse implementation of a solved problem. | A narrow, named need: one compression level with fixed tables (zstd level 1 is LZ77 plus FSE with predefined tables, which is the lz4-encode ticket plus FSE), or a decoder-only requirement for untrusted input (the zstd-decode ticket). Each reopens one row, not the category. |
| Systems: databases, dataframes, tensor compilers (SQLite, DuckDB, Polars/Explorer, XLA/EXLA, LibTorch) | exqlite, duckdbex, explorer, exla, torchx | The value is the library: query planners, columnar engines, autodiff, device backends. defk is a kernel, not a system. | Interop, not rewriting: zero-copy views over their packed buffers (Explorer series and Nx binary-backend tensors are contiguous native arrays; an Arrow buffer is a [f64]/[i64] view) so a custom per-element loop beside them runs as a kernel instead of a Rustler UDF. docs/research/nx-boundary.md says where that line is; file an interop ticket when a workload asks for it. |
| Kernel-owned mutable state (SortedSet, in-place sketches, streaming decoders) | sorted_set_nif, xxh3 streaming, zstd streaming | Not a rewrite question but a semantics one: ADR-0001 keeps state as values. See the kernel-owned-state epic for where exploration stops. | That epic's design review. |

Done when: the table is in examples/README.md, the verdict's Limitations cites it, and each row names its condition in one sentence.
title: Document the rewrite boundary: what we will not write from scratch, why, and what would change it
